questions.text: What data-custody, hosting, segregation, retention, deletion, and exit/transition evidence will a future procurement require?

Which current and future submission standards, code sets, schema versions, and change-management obligations should be treated as controlling?
What source-lineage, transformation, reconciliation, completeness, quality, and reproducibility evidence must be retained and auditable?
What API, extract, researcher, agency, public-use, and interoperability surfaces are expected, with what authorization and portability constraints?
What accuracy, accessibility, methodology, refresh, regression, and explanatory requirements apply to consumer-facing transparency tools?
Which analytic workloads, dashboards, benchmark methods, reproducibility expectations, and policy-use cases should be supported?
Which security/privacy frameworks, independent assessments, incident duties, access controls, encryption, logging, and data-use constraints will be mandatory?
What availability, recovery, support, incident, defect, data-quality, and performance service levels will be measured?
What incumbent transition, parallel-run, knowledge-transfer, portability, source/documentation escrow, and exit criteria should future bidders plan for?
Which cost units and pricing structures does the State want compared: implementation, ingestion, storage, analytics, users, support, enhancements, transition, or outcome/service levels?
